pr_title: kubelet: When apiserver is down, kubelet should restart static pods
pr_body:
HandlePodCleanups is responsible for restarting static pods for the
pod worker after the following sequence:

static pod with UID 1 created
static pod with UID 1 deleted from disk
static pod with UID 1 still terminating in pod worker
static pod with UID 1 recreated on disk

because we know what pods should be running but aren't. However,
HandlePodCleanups doesn't run when one or more config sources aren't
ready such as when the apiserver is partitioned. Since static pods
might be used to self-host the apiserver, we need to ensure a failed
static pod restarts even when the apiserver is down.

Have HandlePodCleanups() run even when some sources are not ready,
but only perform pod worker sync and pod restart functions. The
other cleanup duties (resynchronizing kubelet with the container
runtime) can't be performed without knowing what sources those
resources are attributed to.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.

-->
Fixes #105543

Does not fix the fact that static pods don't get housekept when the apiserver is down for extended periods.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

We need an e2e test that verifies the behavior of static pods when an apiserver config source is down.

issue_context.title: kubelet does not restart static pods when apiserver is down
issue_context.body:
HandlePodCleanups is responsible for restarting static pods, but handle pod cleanups will not run until the apiserver reports in.  If the apiserver or any components it depends on is running as a static pod, it is possible for the static pod to never restart.

Reproduce:

1. Start a cluster
2. Run a static pod with a static UID on a node
3. Terminate the apiservers
4. Restart the kubelet of the node with the static pod
5. Change the configuration of the static pod on disk

Expect: static pod with static uid should restart

HandlePodCleanups should be able to SyncKnownPods to pod worker and restart static pods independent of whether the apiserver is running.

We are missing e2e tests that simulate down apiserver and stress static pods, which could have caught this.

review_comments: Should we consider logging here that we're running without sync'd sources? - Could potentially help with future debugging (i.e why is some stuff working and some stuff broken)

Since adding static pod restart logic in housekeeping brings so many unfriendly changes, should we consider move that to pod_worker?  Maybe we can add a TerminatedCallBack func for pod_worker(after pod's terminated status comes, recheck restart flag and call TerminatedCallBack ), we don't depend on the 2s housekeeping to do pod restart things. it should be pod_worker's responsbility.

The pod worker is responsible for running a single pod to execution.  When a static pod with the same UID changes on disk, it is not the same pod execution (it's a net new invocation).  The decision was to do it in pod housekeeping because only the housekeeper provides the reconciliation behavior to the pod worker.  The real fix is to make the config loop be a proper reconciler, which this takes a step toward.  I do not think adding it to pod worker will make it more maintainable or more correct because then the pod worker would have to track multiple versions of a pod at once, which is duplicating the responsibility of the pod config loop.

Is the idea that `syncState` would be the output of `SyncKnownPods` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76694983a1c50532206504e2b5e2b9767851354e/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1038 if it were run?
